title: Logging a set
question: What happens when I tick a set on the Active workout screen?

actors.label: Lifter
actors.role: Ticks the done box on a set row.
Draws one set and reports the tick to the screen.
Hands the tick to WorkoutService, shows errors and starts the rest timer.
Flips the set to done after validating it, and saves the active workout.
Reads and writes the in-progress workout under the activeWorkout key.
Checks reps 1-999 and weight 0-1000 kg; returns a message or null.
Gives the time stamped on the set as completedAt.
Wraps data in a versioned envelope and talks to localStorage.
Supplies defaultRestSeconds, read when the screen renders.
Shows the countdown and what comes next.

steps.say: The lifter taps the tick on a set row. SetRow calls onToggleDone, which runs toggle() in src/ui/screens/ActiveWorkoutScreen.tsx:90.
The screen asks WorkoutService to toggle that set, by exercise block id and set id.
The service loads the active workout from the repository; with none it throws 'No workout in progress.'
The set is not done yet, so the service validates its weight and reps first.
Valid: the set becomes done and gets a completedAt time from the clock.
The changed workout is saved as the active workout, wrapped as { schemaVersion: 1, data }.
The service returns the workout and nowDone. The screen stores it and clears any error on that set.
Because nowDone is true and defaultRestSeconds (from Settings) is above 0, the screen starts a rest countdown.
The overlay counts down each second and names the next unticked set. The lifter can add or cut 15 s, or skip.
The lifter ticks a set with 0 reps.
The screen asks the service to toggle it, and the service loads the active workout.
Validation fails: 'Reps must be at least 1. Nice try.'
The service throws a ValidationError on the reps field before anything is saved.
The screen catches it and shows the message under that set row. No rest timer starts.
Editing the weight or reps clears the error, so the lifter can fix it and tick again.
